title: 3720. Lexicographically Smallest Permutation Greater Than Target

examples.explanation: The permutations of s (in lexicographical order) are "abc", "acb", "bac", "bca", "cab", and "cba". The lexicographically smallest permutation that is strictly greater than target is "bca".

The permutations of s (in lexicographical order) are "eelt", "eetl", "elet", "elte", "etel", "etle", "leet", "lete", "ltee", "teel", "tele", and "tlee". The lexicographically smallest permutation that is strictly greater than target is "eelt".
The permutations of s (in lexicographical order) are "aabb", "abab", "abba", "baab", "baba", and "bbaa". None of them is lexicographically strictly greater than target. Therefore, the answer is "".
